## Verdicts (plan §)

| # | rule | numbers | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | at 640 L0 recall(<48 px bins pooled) <= 0.5 x recall(>=96 px bins pooled) | 0.004 vs 0.969 (ratio 0.00) | PASS |
| R2 | recall gain 960 vs 640 (absolute) largest in a <64 px bin | gains: <32 +0.001, 32-48 +0.006, 48-64 +0.126, 64-96 +0.213, 96-160 +0.016, >=160 -0.000; largest = 64-96 | FAIL |
| R3 | relative recall drop L0 -> L3 at 640 largest in a <64 px bin | drops: <32 +0.722, 32-48 +0.479, 48-64 +0.469, 64-96 +0.324, 96-160 +0.085, >=160 +0.031; largest = <32 | PASS |

Interpretation choices where the plan is silent: R1 pools the persons of the two bins on each side; R2 compares absolute recall gains (points of recall); R3 uses the relative drop as the plan says; bins with zero L0 recall would be skipped (none occurred if every bin has a number above).

## Notes and threats (added by hand after the run; the numbers above are generated)
- **R2 depends on how "gain" is read.** In absolute recall points the largest 960-vs-640 gain is in the 64-96 px bin (+0.213), so R2 FAILS as I read it. In relative terms (recall960 / recall640) the largest is the 48-64 px bin (0.182 / 0.057 = 3.2x; 32-48: 1.9x; <32: 1.9x; 64-96: 1.35x), which would pass. The plan does not say which; I chose absolute before looking at the numbers and report the other reading here as post-hoc.
- **The cliff is steep.** At 640 L0 recall is 0.001 / 0.007 / 0.057 for people <32 / 32-48 / 48-64 px, 0.613 at 64-96 px and 0.96-0.99 above 96 px. 40% of all reference people (58,090 of 187,021) are under 48 px, so most of the "edge recall" gap (EXP-009 D1) is people the detector essentially never reports at this resolution; 480 -> 960 only moves the 48-64 bin from 0.020 to 0.182 and 64-96 from 0.348 to 0.826.
- **Matcher bias (threat).** The reference box is the keypoint min/max (tight around joints); a YOLO person box is looser. For small people this padding is a larger share of the box, so the IoU >= 0.3 rule is harder to meet exactly where recall is reported as ~0. The rule is frozen and shared with D1, so numbers are comparable to EXP-009, but the absolute recall for the smallest bins may understate detection of *something* near those people. Not tested here.
- **Reference people are AlphaPose outputs**, not hand labels: very small "people" may include false positives of the reference detector.
- Darkness (R3): relative drop L0 -> L3 at 640 is 0.72 (<32), 0.48, 0.47, 0.32, 0.085, 0.031 (>=160): it falls monotonically with height, so the largest drop is in the smallest bin. Bins <32 and 32-48 have a tiny base recall (0.001, 0.007), so their relative drops rest on 36 and 217 found people.
